title: Ain't No Half-Steppin'
year_note: The year is the original's. This recording is an AI-made soul cover posted on YouTube, and its upload title is all we know about it.
album: YouTube upload; the original is on Long Live the Kane

titles: Big Daddy Kane - Ain't No Half Steppin' (1950's Soul Version)

notes.made: Marley Marl produced it for Cold Chillin', working the way the Juice Crew did: Kane brought in the records he wanted and Marley built the beat on a sampler. It takes from three places, Heatwave's 'Ain't No Half Steppin'', ESG's 'UFO' and the Emotions' 'Blind Alley', a Stax-era Volt track produced by Isaac Hayes and David Porter. Kane said Marley didn't like the song at first because it piled up so many samples.
notes.context: Long Live the Kane came out on June 21, 1988, Kane's debut, and went gold in 1989 after peaking at number five on the R&B album chart. The single only reached 53 on the Black Singles chart, but it is the record rappers kept quoting: Nice & Smooth, Biggie, Jeru the Damaja and MF Doom all sampled it. Rolling Stone put it at 25 on its 2012 list of the greatest hip-hop songs.

listen_for.note: The Emotions' 'Blind Alley' loop, a Chicago sister group's soul record, so a soul arrangement is going back to the source.
The title comes from Heatwave's record of the same name, a soul-funk band's phrase, which gives a singer something to hold.

leads_to.title: Blind Alley
leads_to.why: The David Porter song on the Volt album Untouched that runs under Kane's verses, and one of the most sampled soul records there is (Mariah Carey's 'Dreamlover' uses it too).

notes.unverified: Title corrected to the hyphenated 'Ain't No Half-Steppin''. Untouched is dated 1971 in its Wikipedia infobox and reissue copy but 1972 elsewhere on Wikipedia; I used 1971. I couldn't confirm which part of each sample lands where in the track (WhoSampled was blocked), so the listen_for notes stay general.

culture.title: Rolling Stone's number 25
culture.line: Rolling Stone ranked it 25th on its 2012 list of the 50 greatest hip-hop songs.

culture.title: Sampled down the line
culture.line: Nice & Smooth, Ed O.G. & Da Bulldogs, the Notorious B.I.G., Jeru the Damaja, Elzhi and MF Doom all sampled it.
